phase_0.boundary_condition: The fired clay disc as a closed topological ring — the continuous spiral from edge to center on Side A and Side B, fused into a single cycle by the stamp occurrence map, Linear A semantic anchor, and phonetic values, with every impression bijected to a text position.

⊢.chosen_element: raw unfired clay disc with 45 stamp types before impression
⊢.justification: Void state: the substrate and stamp inventory exist but carry no spiral sequence; no positions, no sides, no phonetic values.

⊣.chosen_element: completed disc ring with fused linguistic text
⊣.justification: Terminal anchor: the disc as a closed cycle where spiral terminus meets origin, every impression traced to exactly one phonetically grounded text position, stamp occurrence map and Linear A anchor sealed.

≻.chosen_element: spiral progression from edge to center
≻.justification: Forward morphism: each impression advances the spiral one position inward; the 241/242 positions form a directed path on both sides.

≺.chosen_element: reverse verification from center to edge
≺.justification: Contravariant morphism: verification pass reading the spiral outward, applying Linear A anchor backwards to confirm phonetic assignments and occurrence bijections.

⋈.justification: Composition: each of the 45 distinct stamps composes into the 31/30 segments on Side A/B via the stamp occurrence map; Linear A anchor composes stamp types to phonetic values.

⊙.justification: Self-reference: each physical stamp is identical to itself across all 241/242 impressions; the 45 stamp types are fixed points under IMSCRIB.

∈.justification: The single spiral forks at the disc midline into two arms: Side A (122 positions, 31 segments) and Side B (119 positions, 30 segments). This is the genuine either/or — the spiral must choose which side to inscribe at each revolution.

∋.justification: Reconstitutes the split spiral arms into the original continuous stream. The graviton-repaired probe template [01·graviton·02·45] provides the local repair rule that closes the fork topologically.

⊤.chosen_element: confirmed phonetic value from Linear A anchor
⊤.justification: Affirmative arm: a sign position receives a unique phonetic value grounded in the Linear A semantic anchor (zero-distance theorem) and stamp occurrence map.

⊥.justification: Negative arm: a sign position has no unique Linear A mapping, conflicts with stamp occurrence map, or fails segment boundary consistency.

⊞.chosen_element: sign with multiple simultaneous phonetic possibilities
⊞.justification: Paradice held: homophonous stamps or polyvalent signs where Linear A anchor yields both T and F simultaneously — held as B without resolution.

⊡.chosen_element: permanent clay firing fixing the complete deciphered text
⊡.justification: Irreversible fixation: the kiln firing locks the spiral stream with all phonetic grounding, segment boundaries, and occurrence bijections into ceramic; no further edits possible.
